docsPromises.evidence:
Independently recomputed the fingerprint from scratch with a standalone script (ts.createSourceFile + ts.createPrinter({removeComments:true}) + sha256, not copy-pasted from either pinned file): got a4330bff3e0e420b56c4352ca5b449ae3438f2dae883e1fc59db2201bcade37d, matching BOTH the new pin in retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke.ts:384 AND verify-process-fact-contract.mjs:1897 -- verified against live ground-truth source, not merely internal cross-consistency. Independently confirmed the re-approval basis rather than trusting the commit message: `git diff main...HEAD -- packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts | grep 'import(\|require('` returns zero hits; the full diff of this file (~20 changed lines) is entirely brand strings / readBrandEnv conversions / a bin-name check, with no touches to loader, import, or path-producer logic; and the actual loader call site (initPath construction + `await import(\`file://${initPath}\`)`) is byte-for-byte identical between main and HEAD via direct diff (exit 0), with only its line number shifting (808/809 on main -> 813/814 on HEAD). Both coupled copies did move together in the single commit 83eefb9a10 as required.

Judgment on whether this warranted human re-approval rather than the implementer's own judgement: I consider the implementer's self-approval ADEQUATE here, not insufficient. The fingerprint algorithm fingerprints the WHOLE enclosing file by construction (a documented, known property of this specific guard, already the subject of the F-057 lesson), so ANY edit to cli-engine.ts -- however narrow -- moves the digest; the guard's own purpose is to force a human-equivalent look at the diff before accepting a new digest, not to freeze the file. The implementer did exactly that: checked the diff for import/require/path-producer changes BEFORE repinning (not after), found none, and I independently reproduced the same finding via direct diff inspection. This is a mechanically narrow, low-risk class of change (diagnostic-string / env-name only) verified by an independent reviewer (me) after the fact using the same evidence trail the implementer used. I do not think this rises to needing a human in the loop beyond what the story's existing reviewer-verification chain (this delivery review) already provides.

docsPromises.evidence: Verified the coordinator's central claim from first principles rather than trusting the comment. Confirmed pre-rename main genuinely writes the literal 'lattice acceptance_basis_generate' at acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:347 (git show main:...). Confirmed this branch's writer and verifier are mutually consistent, both using the canonical 'proof-or-stop ...' form. Traced the actual failure mechanism precisely: `generatedBy.command` feeds TWO independent checks -- (a) an exact-match shape check (AT_ADAPTER_RESULT_INVALID) that COULD in principle be widened to accept both spellings without any digest inconsistency, since it is decoupled from the self-consistency digest check; but (b) `acceptanceCoverageBasisSemanticDigest()`, used for continuity comparisons across a basis's own regeneration lifecycle (`expectedBasisSemanticDigest` in 5 call sites in handlers/proofstory.ts, all comparing a freshly-derived semantic digest against a previously-read one), digests the WHOLE basis object including generatedBy.command. I live-reproduced this with the actual compiled acceptanceCoverageBasisSemanticDigest(): two otherwise byte-identical basis objects differing ONLY in generatedBy.command ('lattice ...' vs 'proof-or-stop ...') produce genuinely different semantic digests (sha256:fa992b4f... vs sha256:547d358f...). This proves that widening only the exact-match check would NOT fix the underlying problem -- the semantic-digest continuity check would still diverge independently. CONCLUSION: I agree with the coordinator's judgement. This is a case where the digest-safety argument holds up under adversarial scrutiny, not just plausible-sounding prose; regenerating the artifact (not widening the check) is the correct migration path, and documenting this as an intentional non-read-both exception is the right call, not a deferred fix.
